source.title: Toward Understanding In-context vs. In-weight Learning
source.authors: Bryan Chan; Xin-Yi Chen; A. György; Dale Schuurmans

record.tranche_reason: The study tests how in-context learning changes with data distributions, dataset size, and fine-tuning, using behavioral measures rather than the original induction-head mechanism or phase-change measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper describes its simplified in-context predictor as induction-head-inspired, but it does not identify or causally test induction heads. It does not measure loss by token index or a training-loss bump. Its relevant results measure in-context prediction on synthetic and Omniglot tasks and responses to prompts after Gemini Nano fine-tuning. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study does not identify induction heads. It does measure whether in-context learning emerges and persists, and how that depends on data and training: dataset size, input noise, class frequency and count, context relevance, training steps and fine-tuning. That is the ICL-persistence part of V5. The ICL tested is a context-label copying task built on a stylized induction-head predictor.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors stress that the learnability of the data, rather than distributional properties alone, decides whether ICL or IWL is used. ICL emerges where IWL is not possible and fades as IWL becomes accurate. Persistence depends on the relative difficulty of ICL and IWL, and ICL can be non-transient. Fine-tuning Gemini Nano to memorize facts can override ICL.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates in-context prediction and its dependence on data, training size, and fine-tuning; it does not reproduce the original induction-head measurements or mechanistic analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: ICL outcomes vary with input noise, number and frequency of classes, context length and relevance, dataset size, training duration, and fine-tuning prompts.
record.problems: Most synthetic and Omniglot outcomes are presented in figures without tabulated numerical values. The real-LLM demonstration uses one model, a small memorization fine-tune, and a limited set of prompts; it does not identify induction heads.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows from the cited prior-work results were included. Figure-only parameter sweeps in Appendices B.1.1–B.1.2 are not separately itemized where the text does not state a condition-specific outcome; the text reports the aggregate trends, including variation in class balance, label noise, context sampling probability, context length, and number of relevant examples.

untested.parts: Whether and when induction heads themselves form (no head identification or causal test).
All parts; no previous-token or induction-head composition analysis.
All parts; no formation timing, loss bump or token-index ICL.
All parts; GRU and stylized models show ICL trends but no induction heads are identified.

missing.what: Attention visualization: first-layer attention falls on the context label at N=2^10 (ICL) and on the query at N=2^20 (IWL). This is a mechanistic correlate of the data-dependent shift.
The GRU and the stylized gated model show the same data-dependent emergence and transience of ICL; ICL is persistent at high input noise.
Omniglot held-out images: the transformer performs ICL on CL at first, then shifts toward IWL as N increases.
Longer prompts and different decoy cities change whether the fine-tuned LLM follows the context.

record.verdict_notes: Rows are rated for V5's dependence claim, not for ICL strength. ICL here is copying a matching context label, close to the induction-head pattern, but no heads are identified. Most outcomes are figure-only. The LLM test covers one model and 8 prompts.

versions.untested_parts: No test of head composition with a previous-token head or the [A][B] … [A] → [B] copying mechanism.
No measurement of induction-head formation over training, abruptness, a token-index ICL gain, or a training-loss bump.
No attribution of most large-transformer ICL to induction heads and no loss-by-token-index measure.
Experiments across architectures and model settings measure ICL behavior, not the presence of induction-behavior heads across model families, sizes, runs, or modalities.
Does not test how induction heads themselves form; the real-LLM test is a small fine-tuning experiment on one model and a particular prompt task.
Does not compare few-shot task learning mechanisms or establish that other heads or mechanisms are its main carriers.
Does not track induction-head sub-steps or test whether their formation involves multiple transitions.

rows.subject: Gemini Nano 1 fine-tuned
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned to memorize eight name-city associations, then evaluated with contradictory in-context city information

conditions.value: Short prompt stating each person lives in Kjheergg

rows.measure: Responses and relative log-probabilities for the in-context city versus memorized answer
rows.baseline: Base Gemini Nano 1; authors state it always answers with the in-context city in this test
rows.value: The fine-tuned model reverted to the memorized answer in some cases; in other cases it followed the context or produced another answer. Table 3 reports per-answer relative log-probabilities.
rows.note: The authors report increased probability for memorized answers after fine-tuning, alongside cases where the model still follows the context. The individual results are listed separately in Table 3.
rows.check: The value can be made specific from Table 3. Of 8 identities, the fine-tuned model gave the memorized answer for 2 (Trrrrqe→Qtbnaaa, Kaitlyn→Kingston) and garbled answers for 2 (Kxxh, Kjee). It followed the context for 4. The base model followed the context for all 8.

source_check.correct: State for V5: observed. Table 3 yields base context-following 8/8; fine-tuned context-following 4/8; memorized answers 2/8 (Trrrrqe→Qtbnaaa, Kaitlyn→Kingston); other outputs 2/8 (Cxx1h→Kxxh, Wiesa→Kjee).
source_check.problem: Partial context-following after fine-tuning demonstrates the training dependence V5 predicts; V5 does not require complete loss of ICL.

relationships.condition: Small 2-layer transformers on synthetic and Omniglot data, varying N, noise, class frequency and count, context relevance, and training steps
relationships.reason: ICL emergence and persistence change with these data and training properties: transient at σ=0.2, persistent at σ=0.4, absent with one relevant context, persistent with all contexts relevant (R1-R11).
relationships.display_finding: In-context learning was transient at σ=0.2 and persistent at σ=0.4; it was absent with one relevant context but persistent when all contexts were relevant.

relation.reason: Its own transformer experiments measure how ICL changes with data properties, dataset size, training duration, context relevance, and memorization fine-tuning.

tranche.reason: The study tests V5's behavioural ICL emergence and persistence component through distributional manipulations and fine-tuning, using different methods and measures from induction-head identification.

source_check.notes: The study tests behavioural ICL dependence, not induction-head formation or token-index loss. Dataset-size sweeps and gradient-update sweeps are separate experiments; their conditions should remain distinct.

statements.correction: Synthetic L=4, Lrelevant=1: no ICL. Synthetic Figure 21, L=1, prelevant=1, sigma=0: persistent ICL over millions of updates. Omniglot Figure 21, L=2, one relevant example per sequence: ICL degrades but does not disappear. Table 3 counts: base context-following 8/8; fine-tuned context-following 4/8; memorized answers 2/8; other outputs 2/8.
statements.problem: The absence with one relevant context needs the L=4 condition: the L=1 synthetic experiment has one relevant context and persistent ICL. Omniglot's extended-training experiment has only half its context examples relevant.

statements.correction: Section 3.1: ICL measured by 0-1 error on OOBD examples with relevant context, using cyclically shifted labels. Appendix B.4, Figure 20: additional held-out-image evaluation within existing classes. No token-index loss measure. Gemini Table 3: context-following 8/8 before fine-tuning and 4/8 afterward.
statements.problem: This study's principal ICL evaluation does not use held-out classes; it cyclically shifts labels within the existing high- and low-frequency class sets.
